physics.matter-state-recall-kb.0001.all: energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 °C

physics.radioactivity-atoms-describe-kb..a: small dense positive nucleus of protons and neutrons; electrons orbit in shells; mostly empty space
physics.radioactivity-atoms-describe-kb..b: place GM tube near source connected to counter; count over measured time, count rate = counts/time; subtract background

physics.radioactivity-atoms-explain-kb.0.a: gamma weakly ionising (EM wave, no charge/mass) so loses energy slowly; alpha strongly ionising so loses energy quickly
physics.radioactivity-atoms-explain-kb.0.b: unstable; neutron changes to proton plus electron emitted, giving more stable n:p ratio
physics.radioactivity-atoms-explain-kb.0.c: same number of protons (same element); different number of neutrons

physics.radioactivity-atoms-mcq-kb.0014.b: a fast-moving electron from the nucleus

physics.radioactivity-atoms-recall-kb.00.all: atoms of same element with same number of protons but different number of neutrons

physics.radioactivity-halflife-explain-k.a: beta partly absorbed by foil; change in thickness changes count rate detectably (alpha all absorbed, gamma all passes)
physics.radioactivity-halflife-explain-k.b: background radiation always present; subtract background count rate
physics.radioactivity-halflife-explain-k.c: contaminated source stays in/on body, keeps irradiating; alpha inside body very ionising

physics.radioactivity-halflife-extended-.a: contamination: radioactive material gets onto/into object; irradiation: exposed to radiation from outside source, does not become radioactive
physics.radioactivity-halflife-extended-.b: half-life: time for activity/count rate (or number of nuclei) to halve. Measure background with no source; place source near GM tube; record count rate at regular intervals; subtract background; plot corrected count rate vs time; read time to halve, repeat for several halvings and average

physics.radioactivity-halflife-recall-kb.b: contamination: radioactive atoms on/in object; irradiation: exposed to radiation, not made radioactive
physics.radioactivity-halflife-recall-kb.c: thickness gauging / sterilising equipment / leak tracing / smoke alarms

physics.radioactivity-nuclear-describe-k.a: U-235 absorbs neutron, splits into two daughter nuclei, releasing 2-3 neutrons and energy; those neutrons cause further fissions
physics.radioactivity-nuclear-describe-k.b: fission releases thermal energy; heats coolant/water to steam; steam turns turbine which drives generator

physics.radioactivity-nuclear-explain-kb.a: fewer neutrons absorbed; chain reaction uncontrolled, rate increases, overheating/meltdown/explosion
physics.radioactivity-nuclear-explain-kb.b: requires extremely high temperature and pressure; hard to achieve/contain, more energy input than output

physics.radioactivity-nuclear-extended-k.b: fission: large nucleus splits, needs neutron, used in power stations, radioactive waste; fusion: light nuclei join, in stars, needs very high T and P, little waste; both release energy and mass converted to energy

physics.radioactivity-nuclear-recall-kb..a: two light nuclei join to form heavier nucleus, releasing energy
physics.radioactivity-nuclear-recall-kb..b: two daughter nuclei; 2 or 3 neutrons (and energy/gamma)

physics.waves-em-explain-kb.0010.a: gamma kills bacteria/microorganisms that cause decay
physics.waves-em-explain-kb.0010.b: X-rays ionising, damage cells/cause cancer; lead absorbs X-rays; repeated exposure

physics.waves-em-extended-kb.0013.a: travel at same speed in vacuum; transverse; transfer energy; can travel through vacuum
physics.waves-em-extended-kb.0013.b: radio waves: broadcasting, long wavelength, diffract/reflect; microwaves: satellite and mobile phones, pass through atmosphere; also cooking - absorbed by water molecules, heating them; infrared: grills/toasters, heats surface, TV remotes; visible/infrared in optical fibres

physics.waves-em-recall-kb.0014.c: sunscreen / sunglasses / cover skin / stay in shade

physics.waves-light-explain-kb.0003.all: light hits the inner surface at angle greater than critical angle; total internal reflection occurs; repeated reflections carry light along fibre

physics.waves-properties-describe-kb.000.all: float a cork/object on water; as wave passes it bobs up and down but does not travel along with wave

physics.waves-properties-explain-kb.0007.a: source moves towards observer between emitting waves; wavefronts bunched up; wavelength shorter so frequency higher (Doppler)
physics.waves-properties-explain-kb.0007.b: v = f λ; f constant so λ proportional to v, so λ decreases

physics.waves-properties-mcq-kb.0002.all: the maximum displacement from the rest position

physics.waves-sound-explain-kb.0004.all: larger amplitude of vibration; sound louder (pitch unchanged)

physics.waves-sound-recall-kb.0012.a: higher frequency of vibration gives higher pitch
